name: v0.81.0
body:
### Added

- **Images and fonts in HTML artboards.** Each design keeps its own store of images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) and fonts (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF), added from the assistant and kept once per content; screens and exports show them, the assistant knows which exist, and SVG and disguised files are refused. On the canvas they arrive as inline data, so the sandboxed screen still reaches no network. (#1163)

- **Named OpenAI-compatible endpoints.** `CHIMERA_ENDPOINTS` lists endpoints by name, base URL (https, or http on this machine) and the variable holding the key; a model written `endpoint/<name>/<model>` goes there with its own base and key, beside OpenRouter, instead of through the global `CHIMERA_API_BASE`. The privacy card, receipts and Usage name the endpoint and its host, and `/api/endpoints` lists and tests them. Part of #1133. (#1162)

- **A connector you name in a message connects for that turn.** With MCP autoload off, a Code turn whose message names a configured, enabled connector (say, "use the VoiceStudio connector") connects just that one, says so, and keeps it for later turns that name it; text from tools, pages or files never switches a connector on, and bots keep their own list. (#1161)

### Fixed

- **Code conversations no longer get cut in half.** Reopening a conversation rewrote its file in place, without a lock and from a read taken before a wait of up to ten seconds, so a reader or a crash in that window saw half a file and turns saved meanwhile were lost; under many parallel turns this damaged several sessions and their backups. Session writes are now atomic, flushed to disk and locked across processes, and the reopen merges only the fields it learned. (#1160)

- **HTML artboards use the design system's fonts, and each one opens its own inspector.** A token's font list was written as one quoted name, so screens fell back to a serif face on the canvas and in exports; and the inspector always showed the first artboard, so a second HTML screen could not reach its tweaks or select its elements. Clicking an artboard or its label now makes it the active one. (#1159)

- **Talking about Chimera Design while coding it no longer opens the canvas.** A message that names the product or asks for something visual is no longer read as a design request when it is plainly engineering work: a code path, a command such as pytest, or words like fix, implement or test. (#1158)

- **A URL connector's card describes what testing it does.** The detail of a connector reached by URL no longer says that testing starts a command or that npx may download a package, and a server on this machine (loopback) no longer carries the "reaches the network" chip. (#1157)

name: v0.80.0
body:
### Added

- **Skill card: do not widen types to silence the checker.** A new pattern card on narrowing a value or handling the missing branch instead of widening an annotation to `Any`, `object` or an unchecked union, translated into every site language. Contributed by @CG-5228. (#1150)

- **Design: watch an HTML artboard form while the model writes it.** A new proposal streams its page into a static preview as it is generated; the preview is sandboxed with no permissions, runs no script and reaches no network, and it gives way to the usual proposal, which is still applied only when you accept it. (#1154)

- **Design: tweaks and side-by-side directions for HTML artboards.** An artboard can declare typed CSS variables (colour, number, choice) that the inspector adjusts without calling the model, each change undoable and validated so no value can inject CSS; and the assistant can propose 2 to 4 distinct directions at once, laid out side by side and never applied until you accept. (#1153)

- **Design: fluid-width presentation and selection kept across reloads.** An HTML artboard with `mode: fill` now fills the screen in presentation (the canvas keeps its stored width, so zoom never triggers its media queries), and the selected element stays highlighted after the artboard reloads. (#1152)

- **Restricted model scripts in HTML artboards.** An HTML artboard may carry one model-written `text/x-chimera` script that runs only on the canvas, in an opaque-origin frame whose CSP admits that block by hash; thumbnails and exports stay script-free. (#1151)

- **Export HTML artboards.** HTML artboards now export to HTML, PDF, PNG and PPTX; the PPTX keeps each text block editable, and every export renders with scripts and network off. (#1149)

- **Edit an HTML artboard element in place.** In Chimera Design, clicking an element of an HTML artboard selects it, and the inspector changes its inline style and text without a model call; each change undoes exactly, and the selection reaches the model as fenced data. (#1148)

- **Chimera Design draws screens as HTML/CSS.** The design agent now writes each artboard as a self-contained HTML/CSS screen, rendered in a sandboxed frame on the canvas; the piece-by-piece operations remain for fine adjustments. (#1147)

- **The design agent can write HTML artboards.** New `write_artboard`, `edit_artboard` and `read_artboard` actions write one screen at a time and revise by exact replacement instead of rewriting the file; design tokens become CSS variables. (#1145)

- **HTML artboards render on the design canvas.** An artboard with an HTML source shows on the canvas, in thumbnails and in presentation inside a fully sandboxed frame with its own content security policy; design tokens become CSS variables. (#1144)

- **Chimera Design artboards can hold an HTML/CSS source.** The first step toward generating each screen as HTML: a validated, allowlisted source per artboard with exact-undo operations. (#1143)

### Fixed

- **The desktop updater no longer ships a vulnerable `zip`.** The updater unpacks Windows updates with `zip`, which moves from 4.6.1 to 9.1.3 and past three advisories: a critical header differential that can overwrite arbitrary files, unbounded symlink targets that can exhaust memory, and an AES authentication bypass. An update was only unpacked after its signature verified, which limited the exposure. (#1156)

name: Chimera 0.79.1
body:
Chimera 0.79.1

## [0.79.1] - 2026-10-28
### Fixed

- **Approving a design no longer fails with "another Chimera process asked this question".** The design approval is answered as a question in its conversation, in the approvals window, the status bar and the Governance list. Only the owner's screen can answer it, and two answers at once record exactly one. (#1139)

- **Chimera Design gets a usable first proposal.** A malformed operation comes back as an argument error the model can fix, each operation shows its shape, a cut-off proposal is detected and asked again with fewer operations, and the first proposal asks for typography, backgrounds and shapes instead of plain text. (#1140)

- **Connectors start on Windows, and the app opens without waiting for them.** A connector whose command passes through a Windows `.cmd` launcher (Supabase through `npx`) no longer breaks on an `&` in its URL; an argument that can't pass safely is refused with the reason. The service opens at once and connects the MCP servers in the background, instead of keeping the app on "Failed to fetch" for up to two minutes. (#1138)

- **Audio and images from connectors arrive as files, not as text the model has to read.** A connector that returns a recording or a picture inline (VoiceStudio's narration, for one) used to fill the model's context with base64 and stop the turn. The file is now saved in the project's `mcp-output/` folder, kept out of commits, and the conversation can play or show it. (#1137)

### Security

- **litellm moves past a security advisory.** The model gateway library is now 1.105.6, out of the range of a high-severity advisory about its proxy server. Chimera uses it as a library, so it was unlikely to be exposed. (#1136)

### Added

- **"Ignore permissions" per project, kept across restarts.** A project's switch covers all its conversations, including new ones; each conversation keeps its own switch too. Turning it on releases the cards already waiting. After a restart a banner names each saved project and conversation and reactivates the ones you confirm with one click; the rest are discarded. Only the desktop screen can turn it on, and turning it off always applies. (#1141)

name: Chimera 0.79.0
body:
Chimera 0.79.0

## [0.79.0] - 2026-10-27
### Added

- **Connect VoiceStudio in one click.** Settings › Connectors lists "VoiceStudio (local)", a local voice studio (cloning, voice design, speech, transcription). The card connects when VoiceStudio is running and says how to install it when it isn't. It names the non-commercial default voice model and the need for consent before cloning a voice. (#1134)

- **Speech, music and video through OpenRouter.** With only an OpenRouter key, the agent can now narrate text (`text_to_speech`), make music or sound effects (`generate_audio`), and make short videos (`generate_video`). `generate_image` reports what each image cost. (#1130)

### Changed

- **"Ignore permissions" covers turns sent through the desktop bridge.** When you turn it on for a conversation on the screen, turns another tool sends into that conversation through the desktop bridge no longer stop for approval. Paired devices and plain API tokens still do, and only the screen can switch the mode. (#1132)

- **A calmer Code screen.** A finished turn shows a short receipt (tool calls, failures, files, server, media, verification) with "show all" for the rest, and big diffs fold. The header keeps what matters and puts every other action in a "⋯" menu. On narrow windows the side panel becomes a drawer. (#1131)

### Fixed

- **Tidier settings and project list.** Usage names runs without a recorded model instead of showing a dash, the Usage, Security and Decisions pages line up with the rest, the project list shows each existing folder once and can remove one, Tasks shows project names, and a schedule whose folder is gone says so. (#1128)

- **Workspace media plays in the conversation.** Audio and video the agent wrote get a player that loads on press, relative image paths show the picture, images are capped in height, the HTML preview uses the full height of its panel, and "Mais recentes" reaches the end of a long conversation. (#1127)

- **Fewer approval cards after a browser hiccup, and the design skill loads again.** A browser action that failed before reading a page no longer marks the turn as having read untrusted content, so harmless commands afterwards stop asking for approval. Reading a skill by name (`skill_view`) no longer fails on every call. (#1126)

- **An approval card no longer outlives the question.** A card whose asking process died (an update, a restart) stayed on screen until a 24-hour sweep, and Refuse could not clear it. A question now leaves the list once its own wait has ended, and an answer to it is not recorded. (#1125)

Also in this release: a `changelog_digest` workflow recipe in `examples/` (#1092, thanks @CG-5228).

name: Chimera 0.78.2
body:
Chimera 0.78.2

## [0.78.2] - 2026-10-27
### Added

- **SVG images are accepted, after validation.** Vector models such as Recraft V4.1 Vector return SVG; Chimera rebuilds it from an allowlist (no scripts, event handlers, external links or entity declarations), saves it as `.svg`, and serves it with a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy. (#1115)

### Changed

- **Google search in your own Chrome follows "Ignore permissions".** With the switch on, searches in the paired, visible Chrome run without a card, still paced (one every 20 s, 30 a day) and stopped at a CAPTCHA. When every search key is out of credit or refused, `web_search` tells the agent to use the browser's Google search instead. (#1116)

### Fixed

- generate_image reports OpenRouter's upstream image errors instead of "no image", names the replacement for the retired gpt-image-1 and gpt-5-image ids, and asks Gemini for a square image. (#1123)

- A browser navigation that failed before any page loaded (for example, a site not yet granted to the Chrome extension) no longer marks the turn as having read untrusted content. (#1122)

- The Chrome extension works on current Chrome again: the download denial no longer fails every action with "Cannot access browser-level commands" (downloads are cancelled by a guard instead), Cancel on Chrome's debugging bar can be undone with "Resume Chimera actions" in the popup, and the popup stops offering Allow for a site already granted. (#1121)

- The deepseek-v4-flash catalogue row reads 0.14 in, the live OpenRouter price, so the cost shown for it is not understated. (#1120)

- Registering the Chrome host checks that its Python can read the OS vault (keyring) and refuses with the exact install command when it cannot; before, the extension stayed "paired, disconnected" with no reason given. (#1119)

- Google search in the paired Chrome works: the extension only attaches to web pages in its own tab group (a group tab left on a `chrome://` page made every action fail with "Cannot access a chrome:// URL"), and the results page is recorded by its URL, so trusted sources apply to it. (#1118)

- The Chrome extension pairing survives desktop app updates: the browser host accepts the app's service from any version folder of its own `service-bin`, instead of only the exact version it was registered with. (#1117)

name: Chimera 0.78.1
body:
Chimera 0.78.1

## [0.78.1] - 2026-10-26
### Fixed

- **Image-only models work through OpenRouter.** FLUX, Recraft, GPT Image and Krea go to OpenRouter's images endpoint with the size parameters each model declares; before, every one of them failed instantly with a bare "image generation failed". Failures now say why (HTTP status and OpenRouter's message). (#1113)

- **The "Ignore permissions" button shows its state and acts at once.** It always read "off" because the conversation list never carried the switch, and turning it on mid-turn only took effect on the next turn. The button now shows the real state, and the running turn's next action is released as soon as the switch is on. (#1112)

- Web search says why it failed: a refused key, an account out of credit (top up at the provider) or a failing provider, and the `auto` mode moves on to the next configured provider instead of retrying a dead one. (#1111)

- A run whose model provider and fallback both time out now ends with a record (cost of the calls already made, reason "provider_timeout", exit code 13) instead of crashing with nothing written. (#1110)

name: Chimera 0.78.0
body:
Chimera 0.78.0

## [0.78.0] - 2026-10-26
### Added

- **Chimera Design draws as the agent works.** The canvas applies the agent's changes batch by batch instead of reloading the whole design, falls back to a full reload when a batch is missing or fails, and shows "Creating…" while the agent draws. (#1107)

- Chimera Design: a title menu (rename, duplicate, export), a share link that opens the design, hand, frame and note tools, zoom as a menu, a full-screen Present mode, and phone, tablet and desktop previews. (#1106)

- **The agent makes images with your OpenRouter key, and you see them in the conversation.** `generate_image` now works with OpenRouter's image models (`CHIMERA_IMAGE_MODEL`, default `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image`) and no longer needs an OpenAI key. Each image is saved to `generated_images/` in the project and appears in the answer. An image a model returns in the middle of a turn is kept instead of lost. Choosing an image model that cannot use tools as the conversation's model no longer fails. The agent can also look at an image it made, when its model has vision. (#1105)

- **Trusted sources.** The owner can list sites (or `*` for every public site) whose content does not restrict the run afterwards, so reading the web no longer turns every later command into an approval. Mail, MCP output and local addresses still count as untrusted. (#1103)

- Chimera Design: the agent submits a design for approval in the conversation (approve, or ask for changes with a note), and project code waits until the current version is approved. (#1102)

- Chimera Design: designs with several screens get an index page generated from the artboards, links between screens, and navigation in the canvas and the preview. (#1101)

- Chimera Design: comments anchored to the canvas, with threads you can resolve, a Comments panel that jumps to the element, and the agent reads the open comments and resolves them when addressed. (#1095)

- **Chimera Design now works like a designer at your side.** When you ask for a visual design, the agent first says what it is going for (concept, palette, typography), lists its plan as a checklist that updates as it goes, and builds the design screen by screen. It does not touch your project's code until you approve the design. The design opens beside the conversation as soon as the agent starts it, the card in the conversation opens it with one click, and the tool list says what happened ("Design: updated"). (#1090)

### Changed

- **"Ignore permissions" now releases every connection.** With the switch on, the agent works directly with git, GitHub, `gh`, MCP connectors (Hostinger, Supabase and others), deploys, uploads and send tools. It still asks before destructive commands, before reading or sending a secret file, and before rewriting the main branch. Listing the MCP servers no longer marks the run as untrusted. (#1104)

### Fixed

- Continuing a conversation right after stopping its turn no longer runs the new turn in the app's default folder instead of the conversation's worktree. That mistake turned every read and edit in the worktree into an "outside the project folder" approval. (#1100)

- **The "Ignore permissions" button in the Code screen works.** Clicking it did nothing: the request was refused, and the screen did not say so. It now turns the mode on and off for the conversation, its label shows which way it is set, and a failure is shown instead of swallowed. (#1094)

- The vitest cache file is no longer tracked, and `node_modules/` is ignored at any level, so running the desktop tests from the repo root no longer dirties the worktree. (#1093)

- **On Linux with the built-in sandbox, a running command can be stopped and its output shows as it comes.** Before, cancelling a command run inside the bubblewrap sandbox did nothing, and its output appeared only when it finished. (#1091)

- **The Tools screen describes the pull-request tool in every language.** Its description was missing from the translations. The tests that guard those descriptions also no longer give a different answer depending on whether the machine running them has the tool switched on. (#1089)

name: Chimera 0.77.0
body:
Chimera 0.77.0

## [0.77.0] - 2026-10-25
### Fixed

- **The desktop app's background service no longer gets stuck half-stopped.** A messaging adapter that had never connected (for example a Discord bot with a wrong token) made the service's shutdown fail partway. The service then stayed running without answering, and the app could not reach it until the process was ended by hand. Each shutdown step now runs on its own, and the service always exits. (#1086)

- **The agent's questions reach you even when it phrases the call loosely.** A question sent with both a heading and a list of questions used to be refused with an error that did not say what to change, and the agent could retry the same call a dozen times without the question ever reaching the screen. The list of questions is now asked, and the extra heading no longer makes the call fail. (#1084)

- **A reply cut off mid-tool-call no longer ends the turn with half a project.** The call that could not be read goes back to the model with a request to retry it. Removing the Tailwind or PostCSS setup from a critical config file (next, postcss, tailwind, vite) is now flagged for review, a project with only a build script is verified by running that build, a project's model now applies in its subfolders, `chimera run -` reads non-ASCII input correctly on Windows, and the background service reserves far less memory. (#1082)

### Changed

- **Claude models now use the prompt cache, so long turns cost far less.** Every call path marks the stable part of the conversation, including the latest tool result, so each step rereads the previous one from the provider's cache instead of paying for it again. It is on by default for Claude models; `CHIMERA_PROMPT_CACHE=0` turns it off. (#1083)

### Added

- **The agent can check a page at phone width before calling it done.** A new browser action measures whether the page scrolls sideways at 375 px (or another width) and names the elements that overflow. It also reports whether the page's CSS actually loaded, so a site that lost its styles is no longer reported as finished. (#1087)

- **The agent can look at the app it is building.** When a Code turn starts a dev server in the background inside the project folder, its browser may open that server's port, and only that one. Reading a page served entirely from that port no longer makes later commands ask for approval; a page that loads anything from elsewhere, or opens a connection elsewhere, is treated as before. Chimera's own ports and other local ports stay closed. (#1085)

name: v0.76.0
body:
## [0.76.0] - 2026-10-24
### Fixed

- **Claude models work in the Code screen again.** With an Anthropic model as the default, every coding turn failed on its first step with an error about a tool's input schema. The question tool's schema used a construct Anthropic's API refuses; it is now a plain object, and a test checks every tool's schema so the problem cannot come back. (#1077)

### Added

- **Each project can have its own model.** A Code conversation uses its own pinned model, then the project's, then the global default, and the turn's receipt says which one was used. Changing the model for one project no longer changes it for conversations in another. When the agent proposes a different model, it can only leave you a card naming the conversation or project it would apply to; nothing changes until you approve it. (#1078)

name: Chimera 0.75.0
body:
Chimera 0.75.0

## [0.75.0] - 2026-10-23
### Added

- **"Ignore permissions", for one conversation at a time.** A switch in the Code composer approves by itself what would become an approval card, and records each one; pushes, publishing, payments, messages in your name, secrets and anything that sends local data out still ask. Only you can turn it on, from the screen, and it switches off when the app restarts. The Code screen now waits for your answer instead of refusing after five minutes; automations nobody watches keep the limit. (#1075)

name: Chimera 0.74.2
body:
Chimera 0.74.2

## [0.74.2] - 2026-10-23
### Fixed

- **With the verify-and-repair loop on, a turn no longer waits an hour after its answer in a large repository.** The "changed after it passed" check read every file of the project one git call at a time; it now compares only the paths that changed, with the same result. (#1073)

- **Code turns no longer flash console windows on Windows.** The background service starts git and other console programs without a console of their own; each of them used to open a window for a moment, and a turn started dozens. (#1072)

name: Chimera 0.74.1
body:
Chimera 0.74.1

## [0.74.1] - 2026-10-22
### Fixed

- **A background service that is stopping can still be found and stopped.** It used to drop its record before it had exited, so the app's update waited on it and `chimera service stop --now` answered "not running" while it was alive. It now stays visible as stopping, ends its background jobs and exits; only `--now` ends running turns, and only after checking it is the same process. (#1070)

### Security

- **GitPython 3.2.1 and OpenTelemetry 1.45.1.** Both are indirect dependencies: GitPython up to 3.2.0 checked a submodule's `.git` path only after cloning into it (GHSA-83vg-56qc-22m7, high), and OpenTelemetry up to 1.45.0 parsed `tracestate` without a bound (moderate). (#1069)

name: Chimera 0.74.0
body:
Chimera 0.74.0

## [0.74.0] - 2026-10-22
### Changed

- **Cutting a release now bumps the Chrome extension's version too.** The manifest, its README and the extension docs move to the new version with the package, so the store always receives a higher version. (#1066)

### Fixed

- **A turn's receipt, undo and "changed after it passed" check now see the whole repository.** They stopped at 5,000 files, so in a large repository edits under most folders were invisible: the receipt said no file changed and undo could not restore them. Inside git they now compare against the commit the turn started from, keep your own pre-turn edits out of it, and say when the history changed under them. (#1067)

name: Chimera 0.73.0
body:
Chimera 0.73.0

## [0.73.0] - 2026-10-22
### Changed

- **The Chrome extension's popup now looks like part of Chimera, in light and dark.** It used to show bare browser buttons; the connection status, the button that allows a site, Stop and the pairing code are now laid out and themed, and follow the system's dark mode. (#1059)

### Added

- **A project can tell Chimera how to prepare and test it.** Besides its verification `command`, `.chimera/verify.toml` can declare a `setup` command (for example installing dependencies). After you approve that exact command, Chimera runs it once when a fresh worktree has no environment, and every turn tells the agent which command tests the project instead of letting it guess. Worktrees the app creates for a project now inherit the project's command permission and approved commands; any other folder still asks for its own. Worktrees created by the app before this version stop inheriting until they are recreated. (#1063)

- **The verify-and-repair loop on the Code screen can now be turned on.** With `CHIMERA_CODE_VERIFY_RETRY=1`, a coding turn checks its work with the project's verification command before it closes, hands a failure back to the agent for up to two repairs (tests stay read-only while it repairs), and can end by saying the test contradicts the request. It was built in 0.71.0 but nothing could switch it on. It stays off by default, and the MCP bridge can ask for it one turn at a time. (#1061)

### Security

- **Before Chimera sends anything from your Chrome, the card shows what will go out and to whom.** For a send, post, purchase, deletion or form submission, the approval card now lists the fields it can read (for example To, Subject and the message body, including Gmail's recipient chips), or the surrounding text when there are none, and says so when it cannot read the page. Text Chimera is about to type is shown too. Password, card and verification-code fields never appear. If a field you approved changes before the click, or a recipient is added, nothing is sent. (#1062)

### Fixed

- **The model catalogue knows glm-5.3-flash's cheaper route.** OpenRouter now quotes it at about $0.007 per million input tokens on one route; the catalogue accepts that reading alongside its earlier ones instead of flagging the price as stale. (#1064)

name: Chimera 0.72.0
body:
Chimera 0.72.0

## [0.72.0] - 2026-10-21
### Added

- **The Chrome extension is ready for the store, and only your own screen hands Chimera your Chrome.** The extension's popup is back (it holds Stop and the per-site permission button, which the previous version had lost), with icons, a reproducible package and a page that states each permission and what happens to page content: it goes to the app and from there to the model provider you configured. A turn opened with the server token alone no longer gets your Chrome; downloads triggered by a page are denied; cancelling Chrome's debugging bar stops everything; replying, sharing, forwarding and inviting ask first; and with the bridge's full control on, an irreversible action or a Google search in your Chrome is still approved only on the app's screen. (#1056)

- **Settings → Browser now controls your own Chrome.** It shows whether the Chimera extension is paired and connected (with the one command to register it), lets you list the sites where Chimera may click and type without asking, turn Google search off or to ask each time, stop the Chimera tabs and unpair. A browser action's approval card can now say "Always on this site", except for payments, sending, deleting and publishing, which always ask. Changing that list, stopping and unpairing need the app's own screen: the server token alone, which any local process can read, is not enough. (#1054)

- **Chimera can click and type in your own Chrome, with trust given per site.** On the sites you list in `CHIMERA_BROWSER_TRUSTED_SITES`, your desktop turns click and type without asking, as Claude in Chrome does; anywhere else each action shows you a card. Buying, paying, sending, deleting, publishing and form submissions still ask on a trusted site; passwords, card numbers, verification codes, payment frames, downloads and uploads are refused outright; at a CAPTCHA it stops and hands you the tab. The extension checks again, just before acting, that the element is the one decided and nothing covers it. One limit is stated plainly: on a site you trusted, a plain element that runs its own script is not recognised as irreversible. (#1053)

- **Google search in your own Chrome, off unless you turn it on.** With `CHIMERA_BROWSER_GOOGLE=ask`, your own desktop turns can search Google in a visible tab of your paired Chrome, and each search first shows you a card, even with approvals set to allow. It runs at a person's pace (one per 20 seconds, five per turn, 30 a day), uses no disguise, and stops and hands you the tab at the first CAPTCHA or unusual-traffic page, without trying again for 30 minutes. Results come back as titles, links and snippets, marked as fetched content. Bots, scheduled jobs and the MCP bridge never get it. (#1052)

### Fixed

- **A flaky test of the worktree prune is deterministic.** Its helper recorded a child process before the child had finished starting, so it sometimes named the parent's command line and the check correctly called the worktree abandoned. No product change. (#1055)

### Security

- **Pairing Chrome is a six-digit code from your screen, and the key no longer reaches the agent's shell.** Settings → Browser shows a one-time code (two minutes, five tries) that you type in the extension's popup. The key goes to the operating system's vault, never into the environment of the commands Chimera runs, and is masked if it ever appears. On Windows the local pipe accepts only your user and the host checks it is talking to the installed Chimera before answering. Unpairing reopens pairing at once. What it does not do, and the docs say so: a malicious program already running as your Windows user can still take the key. (#1057)

name: v0.71.0
body:
Chimera 0.71.0

## [0.71.0] - 2026-10-21
### Added

- **Foundation for browsing in your own Chrome.** A read-only Chrome extension and the engine behind the existing browser tool, so pages read there get the same fence, taint and site list as today. It is not connected to anything yet: the host refuses every request until pairing with the app arrives, and bots and scheduled jobs can never select it. (#1048)

- **While the agent repairs a failed check, it cannot edit the tests.** With verification retries on, test files are read-only during the repair (you can allow it once per turn), and the agent can stop with "conflict" when a test contradicts what you asked instead of bending the test. Edits made through shell commands are still only reported, not blocked. (#1046)

- **Questions from the agent are shorter and do not get lost.** The agent can ask up to four short questions at once; long text is shortened instead of failing. The desktop notifies you only when an approval or question has been waiting a few seconds while you are in another window, once per item, and the bridge always lists what is still waiting for you. (#1042)

- **Turn receipts record the success claims an answer makes.** With verification retries on, the receipt lists phrases like "tests pass" or "concluído" found in the final answer and whether the check backs them. It is a record for measuring, not a new message: on sentences it had not seen, the detector was right only 70% of the time. (#1041)

- **A project can name its own verify command.** `.chimera/verify.toml` declares the command the Code screen runs after a turn. It runs only in a folder you granted shell commands, and only after you approve that exact command once; if the command changes, or the turn edits the file, it asks again or skips verification instead of running it. The approval covers the command string, not what `pytest` or `make` then execute. (#1040)

- **`scripts/mixed_batch_census.py` measures how often a step mixes reads and writes.** It reads your trace logs without changing them. On the first real data it found 1.7% of steps, so running read-only calls of a step in parallel is not worth building yet. (#1033)

- **You can steer a Code turn while it runs.** Press Enter mid-turn and the message reaches the agent at its next step; if the turn cannot take it, it waits in an editable queue and goes out when the turn ends. "Send and stop" ends the current turn and sends your message as the next one. A message is never dropped on the way. (#1032)

- **After a long conversation is compacted, the agent can be given back the files it was working on.** With the new option (off by default), the file being edited, the ones written in the turn and the most recently read — up to five, large ones by path and hash only — are put back right after a compaction, and a file that changed meanwhile is called out. When the agent starts re-deriving what it already had, it gets one short note restating the task and what is done, instead of the warning going only to the log. (#1025)

- **A Code turn can end with a receipt the model did not write.** With `verify_retry` on, the answer ends with a short block built from the turn's own record: the files changed according to the real diff, the check that ran and how it ended (or why it did not run), the retries, and whether undo is available. If the model says the tests passed and the recorded check did not pass, a line says so; the model's own text is left as it is. (#1027)

- **A retried check cannot be made green by deleting or skipping a test.** With `verify_retry` on, if a test is removed or newly skipped while the agent retries, the check that passes afterwards does not count: the turn ends failed, says a test was removed or skipped to make the check pass, and stops retrying. Editing a test is still allowed and recorded. The detector reads the change itself, so a weakened assertion inside a test that still exists is not caught. (#1026)

- **`scripts/verify_census.py` counts how often a Code turn's check passed, failed or did not run.** It reads the stored turn receipts and prints only counts and the reason a check abstained. The first reading, on 190 turns, found no check had ever run: 84 abstained because running on the host was declined and 106 had no check at all. (#1024)

- **A Code turn can check its work before it closes, and hand a failed check back to the model.** Until now the check ran after the turn was closed and the model never saw it, so a turn that broke the tests still ended "done". With the new `verify_retry` option (off by default), a failed check puts its command and a slice of its output back into the same conversation and the agent tries again, at most twice. A check that could not run is reported as "not verified" with the reason, and is never shown as a pass. (#1021)

- **`chimera solve --no-thinking` for models that reason until the output runs out.** A reasoning model such as Qwen3.7 Flash can spend the whole output ceiling thinking and answer with nothing; the option asks it to answer without a thinking phase. It is opt-in, so every other run behaves exactly as before. (#1017)

### Changed

- **"Passed" means the delivered code was the code that passed.** With verification retries on, a check that passed before the agent changed more files reads "not verified" and names the files; two repair attempts that do nothing stop the loop; and an answer the provider cut off is marked partial instead of final. (#1047)

- **Self-improvement keeps its hands off the tests.** A lesson or skill is saved only when it points to the run that shows it, and an attempt that changed tests or the verifier's settings is never learned from — unless whoever started the run explicitly allowed editing tests. (#1035)

- **A sub-agent says how it stopped.** Its answer reaches the main agent with a status line — finished, or cut off and marked incomplete — and its text is treated as data, not instructions. (#1038)

- **A declined command is not asked for again in the same turn.** After you (or the host-execution setting) say no to running a command, the agent is told at once that commands are off for the rest of the turn and carries on without them, instead of piling up approval requests that expire. Allowing commands for the folder mid-turn lifts it. (#1036)

- **Following a turn through the bridge no longer floods the caller.** A job's default answer is a short summary — recent events, the final answer up to 3,000 characters, every cut marked — and it always lists every approval or question still waiting. The full history is one `since` away. (#1034)

- **Knowledge no longer carries a Skills tab, and the Connectors screen is better tested.** The redirect to Settings › Skills shipped in 0.70.0, so the duplicate tab is gone; old `tab=mcp` and `tab=openapi` addresses land on Settings › Connectors. The Connectors tests regain assertions found missing by two independent audits (approval 409 against 503, the held-server cue, key-format cases, an OpenAPI connector that cannot be switched on while broken). (#1022)

### Fixed

- **Closing a conversation cancels a pending "send and stop".** The message no longer goes out after the conversation's screen is gone. (#1043)

- **A connection that drops in the middle of an answer no longer ends the turn.** The interrupted step is sent again once, and a failed tool is retried only when it only reads and the failure was a network hiccup; a permission refusal is reported and not repeated. (#1037)

- **The Code screen's Explorer is governed like the turn it serves.** What it reads is audited, honours your denied tools, and marks the rest of the turn as having read outside content; anything that would need your approval is refused rather than run unasked. (#1039)

- **Usage totals no longer turn "not reported" into zero.** When a provider does not say how many prompt tokens came from its cache, totals now show "not reported" instead of adding a 0 — the old totals could read as no caching at all while each turn's receipt showed most of the prompt cached. Traces also record when the cache stops answering although the prompt prefix did not change. (#1031)

- **A token-leak test no longer fails by chance.** It used random hexadecimal tokens, and five of their characters could match an id in the response; the tokens are now fixed, varied and free of hexadecimal letters, and a control case shows a real leak is still caught. The nightly secret scan no longer flags the fake keys in one test file. (#1029)

- **The model catalogue no longer offers DeepSeek R1, which OpenRouter withdrew.** Where it was a default, the DeepSeek model the catalogue already lists for the same role takes its place, and the live price of `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` is now 0.44 in and 1.32 out per million tokens. The check that compares the catalogue with the provider every day on main was failing on both. (#1028)

- **The stale-consent tests no longer fail on a slow Windows runner.** They compared real latencies on a shared CI machine with an absolute bound; they now check the approval path and that the gap is measured. The pre-registered 1.2-second bound is unchanged and reported by the bench, where 1.2038 seconds still counts as a violation. (#1023)

- **`chimera solve` says "verify abstained" when the check never ran, instead of "failed".** In four runs measured on 19/10 the verify command had asked to run on the host, nobody answered the approval inside 120 seconds, and the run was reported as a failure while the same checks, run by hand, were green. The summary now names how many attempts abstained; the exit code is unchanged. (#1020)

### Security

- **Pillow 13.0.0.** Fixes nine published advisories in the image library, one of them critical. A dependency of the optional benchmark harness had held every install, the desktop app included, on the vulnerable version. (#1050)

- **Security updates for three dependencies.** aiohttp moves to 3.14.4, and the desktop app's certificate checking libraries (rustls-webpki, webpki-root-certs) to versions that no longer trust distrusted intermediate certificates. (#1044)

body:
Chimera 0.70.0

## [0.70.0] - 2026-10-19
### Added

- **The terminal chat now compacts, plans and undoes like the desktop.** `chimera chat` and `chimera assist` compact the context by default with the desktop's policy (`--no-compact` turns it off). `/plan <task>` shows a plan first and runs the task only once you approve it; approving pre-approves no risky action. `/undo N` lists the files of the last N turns, asks, and puts them back through the same durable store the Code screen uses, keeping any file you edited afterwards. Plain `/undo` still takes back the last turn. (#1015)

- **Go back to before any turn of a conversation, from a timeline in its header.** A rewind button opens the points the durable undo kept, with the hour and how many files each touched; choosing one first shows exactly which files would be restored and which would be left as they are because you edited them afterwards, and asks for confirmation. Going back means before that turn — the old restore only undid the turns after the one you picked — and the restore itself can be redone from the same timeline. A turn with no saved copy of any file is shown disabled with the reason. The preview route writes nothing and applies the restore's own rule; neither route is on the desktop bridge, so no paired device or outside client can restore files. (#1014)

- **The Editor marks what git sees, opens files by name, previews HTML and asks before dropping unsaved work.** The file tree shows modified, added and untracked files with a letter and their folders with a dot, from the same git status as the Changes card, refreshed after a save and when an agent turn ends; files carry an icon by type. "No file open" lists recent files for the project and the files changed in this folder, and Ctrl+P opens a file by name. An `.html` file has a Preview toggle in the same sandbox the Code screen uses, showing unsaved edits too — handy for Chimera Design's export. Closing a tab with unsaved changes asks to keep editing, close without saving, or save and close. (#1010)

- **Select code in the Editor and ask Chimera about it, or ask for a change shown as a diff.** A floating bar on a selection (Ctrl/⌘+L to ask, Ctrl/⌘+I to change, in the shortcuts table) takes an instruction in place: "Ask" sends the lines to the project's Code conversation as a `context` item, the same path as an `@` mention; "Change this" adds `propose_change`, which the server runs read-only with one file and line range, so the proposal comes back as an inline diff with Accept and Reject and is never applied on its own — Accept saves through the Editor, and disappears when the lines changed since the request. A file that changes on disk while open is held with its diff and stays read-only until "Keep" or "Undo"; it says "Changed by Chimera" only while a Chimera turn or run is active in the project. The Editor gets a breadcrumb with the project's name and its own status bar (line and column, language, encoding, saved); the conversation's bar leaves the Editor while nothing runs. (#1005)

- **Mention files, folders, designs and conversations with `@` in the Code composer.** Typing `@` opens a keyboard-first list — the project's files and folders (fuzzy), designs and recent conversations — announced to screen readers; a choice becomes a removable chip and travels with the turn as typed context. A file up to 8,000 characters is attached inline, sanitised and fenced as data and recorded in the ledger as a read; a larger one or a folder goes by path for the agent to read; a design by id with a short summary; a conversation by id and title, never its transcript. Absolute paths and `..` are refused before the turn runs, symlinks out of the project and Chimera's own `.env` are refused when resolved, and a guest on a share link cannot mention designs or conversations. `POST /api/fs/paths` lists names inside the workspace for the picker, capped at 20,000 entries. Slash commands work as before, and the first turn's title is the line you typed, not the attached context. (#1003)

- **Chimera Design, part 6: export to PDF, PNG and PPTX, and to a chat as a file.** PDF is the static page printed by Playwright's Chromium, one page per artboard at its size, with JavaScript off and every request that is not `data:` aborted (a test shows the same hostile page runs its script without the guard); PNG is one image per artboard, or a zip of them; PPTX (python-pptx, the `documents-out` extra) puts each element at its frame on a slide per artboard. When Chromium or python-pptx is missing, the export refuses with what to install — nothing is downloaded on its own — and the export dialog shows that sentence. The route and the `design` tool accept the four formats, still behind confirmation and outside the bridge; a linked chat gets PDF by default through the existing attachment rules, never HTML. Images stay placeholders until there is an asset store. (#1002)

- **Chimera Design, part 5: designing beside the conversation on the Code screen.** The canvas opens in the Code screen's centre slot — conversation on the left, canvas on the right, a switch between them on narrow windows with both kept alive. It autosaves through the operations route with a visible state (saving, saved with the revision, conflict, offline); a conflict reloads the server copy and re-applies unsaved edits only when they all still fit. Manual and agent edits share one undo history. A turn that asks for a design shows "Open in Chimera Design" (an explicit ask opens it with the brief), and each change the agent makes shows a card that opens the document. Beside the canvas: propose from a brief (summary, assumptions, checks and a preview of the dry run, applied only when you click Apply), refine the selection, audit, edit the tokens and check the design against them with a jump to each finding, comments per element, versions with restore, and export to HTML — restore and export ask first. The palette has "Open design" and "New design"; the client now deletes a group's children and allows deleting inside a group, as the server does. (#998)

- **Full control through the desktop bridge, switched on from the screen only.** A third bridge switch, "Full control" (`CHIMERA_BRIDGE_FULL_CONTROL`, off by default), lets an outside agent such as Claude Code do through the MCP bridge what today only the screen does: answer approvals and setting suggestions, take owner decisions (folder grants, approval rules, plugins, marketplaces, worktree pruning), call the routes that need `confirm: true` (design restore, delete and export; storage clean-ups; troubleshooting), change the owner's settings directly, and open any screen of the app (`ui.navigate`, checked against the app's own screens). Only the screen credential can turn it on, the bridge and `PATCH /api/config` refuse to, and turning it off takes effect on the next call; while it is on, a bar on every screen says so with a one-click off, and each call made with that authority writes an audit entry with ids only, listed in Settings › Security. Still out of reach with it on: credentials (keys, tokens, OAuth, the `.env`, the Runner), who can reach the app (pairing, sharing, the LAN door, the server token, messaging bots and their allowlists, the bridge's own switches) — and an approval still never overrides a governance BLOCK. With the switch off nothing changes. (#1000)

- **A grid of 27 categories in Discover, on Skills, Connectors and Plugins, with Productivity among them.** Each tile has a line drawing in the theme's ink and the number of items that clicking it would list (search and the other filters applied); an empty category does not appear, the grid shows eight tiles until "Show all", and a pressed tile sets `cat=` in the address, ticks the same box in the filter menu and clears on a second click. Every category value shipped today — the skills catalogue and its topics, the bundled skills, the curated MCP servers — maps to one of the 27, and a test fails the build when one falls through to "other"; the 27 ids are checked against the backend's list and the three public catalogues share the same file. Productivity is new: the reverse-engineering tool rea, the Apple notes and reminders suite, smart home and translation file there instead of security or documents, GitHub files under code, and Firebase under databases next to Supabase. (#992, #994)

- **Chimera Design, part 3: the HTTP routes.** `/api/design` lists, creates and reads design documents, applies validated operations against an expected revision (a conflict answers 409 with the inverse operations), lists versions, checks a document against its tokens, and asks the configured model to propose, refine or audit — a proposal comes back validated and dry-run but is never applied: the screen shows it and applies it through the same operations route. Restore, delete and the HTML export (a download, never a page) require `confirm: true`, and those three stay out of the desktop bridge so no outside client can answer the owner's question for them; the rest are reachable from the bridge at the operate tier. Every change writes an audit event with ids and counts only, model calls are metered under "design", and the storage card counts the `designs` folder. (#993)

- **Chimera Design, part 4: the agent tool, offered when a turn asks for a visual design.** A deterministic detector (Portuguese, English and Spanish, accents folded, whole words) reads each Code turn: naming Chimera Design, asking to use it, or asking for something presented as a design opens it outright; a bare "design" only counts with a visual signal (landing page, slide, banner, mockup, screen…), and code senses such as "design pattern", "system design" or "o design do banco" never fire — 97 cases pinned in a test. Only then does the turn get the `design` tool (create, summary, apply, propose, export to HTML in the workspace), a short note about it in the turn context, and a `design_suggestion` frame; other turns are unchanged and carry no extra schema. The tool obeys the posture (read-only returns a proposal without applying it), never sends HTML to a bot, marks its output as untrusted, stays out of guest turns, and `CHIMERA_TOOL_DENYLIST=design` removes it. (#995)

- **A grid of 26 categories in Discover, on Skills, Connectors and Plugins.** Each tile has a line drawing in the theme's ink and the number of items that clicking it would list (search and the other filters applied); an empty category does not appear, the grid shows eight tiles until "Show all", and a pressed tile sets `cat=` in the address, ticks the same box in the filter menu and clears on a second click. Every category value shipped today — the skills catalogue and its topics, the bundled skills, the curated MCP servers — maps to one of the 26, and a test fails the build when one falls through to "other"; the 26 ids are checked against the backend's list. (#992)

- **Chimera Design, part 2: the document domain.** `chimera/design/` holds the design document (pages, artboards, text, shape, path, image and group nodes, element comments, design tokens) with a schema version and migrations; operations applied all-or-nothing with an inverse for every one, using the same wire names and camelCase keys as the desktop canvas; ids a model proposes for new elements are replaced by server ids; a store under `designs/` with optimistic revisions, the last 50 versions kept and restore as a new revision, never a rewrite; a static HTML export with every text escaped, no script and a restrictive CSP; checks against the tokens (colours, fonts, 4.5:1 text contrast, elements off the artboard); image import checked by magic bytes, SVG refused. The model call (propose, refine, audit) fences the brief, requests and canvas text as untrusted data, asks once more when the JSON does not validate, and dry-runs the operations so an invalid proposal is reported instead of applied. No route or tool yet. (#991)

- **The catalogues carry real dates, GitHub stars with the date they were read, and sections computed on this machine.** `pins.json` now records, at bump time, the first and last commit that touched each item's own content (not its generated card, which every metadata refresh rewrites), so "New" and "Updated" are measured against the pin's date and stay stable. Stars come with `stars_at` and `stars_repo`: the count the pinned catalogue recorded, then a background read of `api.github.com` through the plugin installer's allowlisted fetch, cached 24 hours, never awaited by the route, and off with `CHIMERA_CATALOG_STARS=false`. `GET /api/catalogs/{kind}` adds `sections` — For you (from MCP servers configured, skills installed and the manifests of registered projects, each with its reason, absent without a signal), Works without setup, From the Chimera library, New and Updated; an empty section is never sent, and the schema still has no install counts. (#990)

- **Chimera Design, part 1: the canvas editor.** The desktop gains an SVG design canvas (`components/design/`, `lib/design/`), not yet mounted in a screen: artboards with size presets, text, rectangle, ellipse, line and freehand shapes, comment pins; select, marquee and shift-select, move by drag or arrow keys, resize with eight handles, align with snapping guides, inline text editing, duplicate and delete, zoom anchored at the pointer and pan; undo and redo with a drag recorded as one step. Every shortcut is in one table that both the key handler and the `?` help sheet read, the whole flow works from the keyboard with actions announced to screen readers, and the inspector folds away on narrow widths. Colours come from the document as data and are checked against a strict pattern before they reach an attribute; the design gate gains no exception. No new dependency. (#986)

- **The app reads the public plugin, skill and connector catalogues from pinned commits only.** `chimera/catalogs/pins.json` names each of `brcampidelli/chimera-plugins`, `chimera-skills` and `chimera-connectors` by full commit sha and the sha256 of every file read; the loader fetches only those exact files, checks the hash before parsing (a mismatch is refused and never cached), caps each file at 1 MiB, caches verified bytes per commit so it works offline, and without cache or network returns an empty catalogue with the reason. `GET /api/catalogs/{kind}` serves neutral items (with the same refusal reason the plugin installer gives); nothing updates at runtime — `chimera catalog pins --check` only reports newer commits, and a release bumps pins on purpose (`scripts/bump_catalog_pins.py`). The schema has no install counts, and a test fails if one appears. (#984)

- **One set of catalog components for Skills, Connectors and Plugins.** The desktop gains shared catalog primitives (screen with Mine/Discover, search with the `/` shortcut and a two-step Esc, filter and sort menus kept in the address, sections, cards, status pill, skeleton) and a neutral item model. A card says what an item runs before who made it, keeps a non-installable item visible with the reason, shows a vendor badge only when the catalog flag and the pinned repository's owner both prove it, and sorts by GitHub stars with items lacking data at the end rather than as zero; the model has no install counts, and a test fails if one appears. Nothing uses the screen yet; the next PRs move Plugins, Skills and Connectors onto it. (#983)

- **MCP servers that sign in with OAuth connect natively, registering themselves.** Chimera's HTTP MCP client now discovers the server's authorization server (RFC 9728 / RFC 8414), registers a client dynamically when none is configured (RFC 7591), and signs in with the authorization code and PKCE S256 on a loopback redirect, with the `resource` indicator; tokens are refreshed and stored in the OS keychain (or a 0600 file in the data folder), never in `mcp.json`, logs or routes. Notion, Linear and similar hosted servers work without the `mcp-remote` bridge. A browser sign-in opens only from the owner's screen (Connect) or an interactive `chimera mcp login`; Test, bots, cron and `serve` use stored tokens or say to connect in the app. The agent's read tools and shell refuse the token folder. (#981)

### Changed

- **The Code screen speaks plainly at the top, in the status bar and before the first turn.** "Commands off" is a badge that leads to the folder's setting instead of looking like a button. The status bar names tools in words ("Task list updated" rather than `todo_write ✓`), shows tokens compactly with how much came from the cache ("1.6M tokens (98% cached)") and the cost in the interface language — four decimals below one cent, so a small turn is never shown as zero — and appears only on the Code screen. An empty conversation welcomes you with suggestions from the folder's git state (review the changes, run the tests, explain the project, or set the folder up as a project). The two voice buttons say what each does, and a conversation's title skips a leading "Read …" instruction line when real content follows. (#1013)

- **The Code screen's side panel, part 2: plain words, the whole environment, connectors you can act on, and a calmer layout.** The Memory card says how many memories this turn used instead of "1 recuperado(s) (fts)"; Environment shows the whole approval policy, and says when the conversation is in a worktree and which project it belongs to; each Connectors line has Test and a link to Settings › Connectors, and an OAuth server shows connected or expired with Reconnect. The default order puts approvals and changes first and machine and environment last — an untouched 0.68 or 0.69 layout moves to it, a rearranged one keeps its arrangement — the drag and close controls appear on hover or keyboard focus with no animation, and the status at the top of the panel no longer repeats the status bar. (#1009)

- **Settings › General opens with the basics, Settings can be searched, and the Profile shows what Chimera uses about you.** General now starts with interface language, default project, default model and response style; Voice is its own section, long labels with benchmark figures are a short sentence with "Learn more", and "only for turns longer than (seconds)" is a selector, with a "Custom" entry kept for a stored value that is not one of the presets. A search field (Ctrl/Cmd+K) finds an option by its translated label or description and opens its tab, and the content uses more of the width. The Profile shows the response language saved for the agent (and the interface language when it differs), the response style as read-only with a link to the composer, the registered projects, and the persona facts, editable in place — nothing new is stored. (#1008)

- **Settings › Connectors puts MCP servers and OpenAPI connectors on one catalogue screen.** *Mine* lists both, with what waits for you first (a held server, one that still needs its OAuth sign-in, an OpenAPI connector that arrived switched off); testing, the last result, approving a held change and OAuth connect or disconnect live in the item's detail panel (`item=`). *Discover* shows the curated MCP catalogue, with each server's containment on its capability line, and the pinned public catalogue (`brcampidelli/chimera-connectors`); a curated entry is configured in its detail with secrets in password fields that are never echoed and nothing saved before Add. The "Official vendor" badge now needs proof: each curated entry names its upstream repository, and a test fails the build when an official entry is not published by its vendor's organisation. (#989)

- **Settings › Skills moves onto the shared catalogue screen.** *Mine* opens with the skills active now, then what waits for you (installed but unread, learned and pending), on, off, and the learned skills with their uses and wins; *Discover* has the Chimera library in work order, the pinned public catalogue (`brcampidelli/chimera-skills`) and the third-party catalogue, each card with its portability verdict and licence. A skill's detail panel (`item=`) shows what it is, what reaches the agent (read in place, which also satisfies "read before switching on"), licence, source and commit, and the steps install → read → switch on; checking for an update and uninstalling live there. The old Knowledge addresses and anchors redirect to the matching view and section. The bundled library and the pinned catalogue are both listed, each with its source, rather than one silently replacing the other. (#988)

- **Settings › Plugins moves onto the shared catalogue screen, with a detail panel of its own.** *Mine* groups plugins as Waiting for you (pending and held) first, then On, then Off or denied; *Discover* shows "Work without setup" first and each marketplace after, and an item that cannot be installed stays listed with its reason on the card and as the + button's description. Opening a card shows a side panel at its own address (`item=`): what the plugin is, its source and licence, and the steps install switched off → review → switch on, built on the existing switch-on dialog and update diff. Back and Esc close it and focus returns to the card; a link to an item that no longer exists says so. Switching on stays an owner-only action outside the desktop bridge. (#985)

- **Settings has a Personalization group: Skills, Connectors and Plugins.** The settings column now reads General, Appearance, then *Personalization* (Skills, Connectors, Plugins) and *System* (Connections, Usage, Security, Decisions). Skills moved from Knowledge and the MCP servers and OpenAPI connectors moved out of Connections into Connectors, each screen unchanged for now. Old links keep working: `#/knowledge?tab=skills` and the Connections MCP/OpenAPI tabs redirect to the new places without adding a history step, and the command palette points at them. Group headers are not tab stops and the arrow keys skip them. (#982)

- **Plugins from a subfolder of a GitHub repository install too, and `rounded-card` has its token.** A marketplace entry with a `git-subdir` source pinned to a commit on github.com now installs, downloading only that folder with the usual size, name and link limits; a `url` source pointing at the root of a GitHub repository with a commit sha is read as a GitHub source. Other hosts and unpinned sources stay refused. Thirteen desktop components used `rounded-card` without its token and rendered square; the token exists now and the design gate refuses a utility name with no token. (#979)

### Fixed

- **Five defects found by driving Chimera from outside: titles, long options, "Other", expired questions and commands that are off.** A conversation whose first message named several files took the first heading of the first one as its title — an agent's instruction file won over "T1 · Side panel…"; the heading is now used only when exactly one ordinary file is named in a short message. `ask_user` cuts an option label over 120 characters with an ellipsis and keeps the full text as its tooltip and answer, instead of refusing it and making the agent ask again. Choosing "Other" focuses the text box and sends nothing until there is text. A question that expired while you typed says so and offers "Send as the next message" with your text kept, and the bridge and the screen now agree on whether a turn is running. A turn without commands in its folder is told so up front, and a refused `run_shell` says "commands are off for this folder — ask the owner to allow them" instead of a raw OS error. (#1011)

- **Typing straight after picking an `@` mention no longer scrambles the next word.** Picking a mention removes `@word` from the draft, and the composer put the caret back with a `requestAnimationFrame` that ran unconditionally with the position from the moment of the pick; keys typed before that frame landed at the end of the box and the frame pulled the caret back in the middle, so `@login` became `gin@lo` and the list never opened. It showed only on a loaded machine — or with a fast typist or a busy long conversation — and failed CI three times while passing locally, so #1006's longer wait could not help. The caret is now set in a layout effect in the same commit that writes the draft, only if the box still holds that text; a regression test holds frames back mid-word, and the extra waits are gone. (#1007)

- **Read-only turns run beside each other, and a turn stopped while it waits for its folder never starts.** The rule that a turn with no write tool skips the folder lock existed but reached nobody: the bridge's `desktop_send` accepted a narrower posture only at full control, although the server accepts narrowing at every tier, and with `CHIMERA_DEFER_TOOLS` on the `tool_call` proxy always counted as a writer. A client can now ask for `posture: {reach: "read_only"}` at any tier, the proxy is judged by its catalogue, and writers — MCP tools included — still take the folder one at a time (a reader may see a tree mid-edit; it makes no undo). Stopping a queued turn used to answer "stopping" and leave it listed as running for up to a quarter second, long enough for the bridge to read it; it now leaves the queue before the answer, returns `stopped_before_start`, and starting and stopping decide under the same lock, so a stopped turn never starts. (#1004)

- **A turn survives a dropped connection, a damaged conversation stays listed, and the bridge's job status is short and complete.** A provider connection that drops mid-stream used to end the coding turn with nothing kept; the agent now resends the step twice (1 s, then 4 s), then tries once without streaming through the fallback models, and only then fails with the cause — real refusals (key, credit, context, policy, rate limit) are not retried, and a tool never runs twice. A conversation file that no longer parses was omitted from the list in silence; each save now keeps the previous good copy, a read falls back to it, an unreadable file is set aside instead of overwritten, and a conversation no copy can open is listed as damaged and never deleted. Over the bridge, `desktop_job` without `since` returns a bounded summary (last events, every approval, notice and error, counts per tool, the receipt) instead of the whole turn, pages with `since`, and always shows the turn's pending approvals; context drift becomes a notice in the conversation instead of a log line. (#1001)

- **Knowledge › Profile lists each fact once, and Memory puts the facts first.** The profile route sends the same facts twice — `profile`, the ordered text for the model's prompt with an English suffix, and `persona`, the same facts as records — and the screen drew both; the test mocked a `profile` the real route never returns, so the duplicate never showed in it. The screen now draws one list from `persona`, an unverified fact carries a translated badge, and the model's suffix never reaches the screen; the API keeps both fields for the bridge. Memory opens with the facts and a one-line summary, hides fact types with nothing in them, explains "clean" and "unverified" in plain words (a source Chimera trusts versus outside content), filters to the unverified facts in one click, and names the origin in words. (#999)

- **The Code screen's side panel shows only cards with something in them, and "Background" and "Tasks" are one card.** The empty-card rule knew only the last turn's panels; the rest relied on a CSS rule that does not act on a minimised card or a tab group (and jsdom, which runs the tests, applies no CSS — a test even asserted the empty Background frame was there). One rule now decides "empty" for the card and the panel alike, for every card, open, minimised or tabbed; Context, Connectors (none configured), Changes (clean or not a repository) and Background disappear when empty, and when every card is empty the right column goes too. "Tasks" listed the same jobs as "Background": Background keeps its stop button and output and now also shows the turn queue, and saved layouts that held Tasks hand its place to Background. A guard renders every card empty in the default, all-minimised and all-tabbed layouts and fails if one shows. (#997)

- **Smaller fixes on the Code screen: empty projects, the composer's settings, the palette, wrapping and search.** A registered project with no conversations starts collapsed and, opened, says so with a "Start one here" button, instead of an open header over nothing. The composer's settings block opens for one visit and closes when a turn starts; "Keep open" is the remembered choice (a block left open by the old behaviour is closed once), and the no-sandbox warning stays outside it. The command palette lists the eight most recent conversations and searches all of them, archived ones marked, opening the one chosen. The file viewer has a wrap toggle remembered per kind of file, and a search result in the Editor opens the file at its line. (#996)

- **The catalogue price of `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` follows OpenRouter to 0.10 in / 0.30 out per million tokens.** The live check on main read the input nine times dearer than the row's 0.0108; the row is what a receipt falls back to when the live index is unreachable, so it now carries the live pair and 0.0108/1.28 joins the figures already seen. (#987)

name: v0.69.0
body:
### Added

- **Markdown prompt commands in the Code composer, and Markdown agents listed in the app.** Typing `/` lists the commands of the project, your own and those of active plugins; `/name args` expands on the server with the CLI's rules, nothing executes, built-in commands keep priority, and a plugin command marks the turn as tainted. Automation › Agents lists Markdown and plugin agents read-only with their source, model and effective tools; they still run from `chimera solve --subagents`. (#977)

- **A Code conversation knows the repository and branch of its folder.** At the start of each turn the conversation records its project (the repository's main checkout), branch and whether the folder is the main checkout, a git worktree or a plain folder, read from the git files without running git. The record survives the worktree's removal, and the session list exposes it so the sidebar can group a repository's worktrees under the repository. (#965)

- **Chimera reads Claude Code plugins and marketplaces as data.** `chimera.plugins` reads a plugin directory (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP and LSP servers) and a `marketplace.json`, and classifies each component by what it would do: text only, start a local process, reach the network, or run commands. Nothing is installed, imported, executed or downloaded; only pinned sources (a local path, GitHub with a commit sha, an https archive with sha256) are installable, and problems carry stable codes compatible with `claude plugin validate`. (#966)

- **Clean up a project's finished worktrees from the Code sidebar.** A dialog lists every worktree of the repository with the reason each one is kept (main checkout, in use, dirty, unmerged, created outside Chimera...), previews the removal and removes only what the preview listed, with `git worktree remove` without `--force` and `git branch -d`. Only worktrees Chimera created can be removed there; their conversations are archived, never deleted, and the MCP bridge can list but never prune. (#967)

- **Code conversations get readable titles, and you can rename them.** The title follows your own name for it, then a title the caller passed (the MCP bridge's `desktop_send` takes `title`), then the first `#` heading of a Markdown file the first message cites inside the workspace, and only then the first message. Rename with the pencil on the row or F2; an empty name returns to the automatic one. No title is generated by a model. (#968)

- **Install Claude Code plugins — disabled until you switch them on.** `chimera plugin install` takes a local folder, a GitHub repository pinned to a commit sha or an https archive with its sha256; the plugin lands in `<home>/plugins` as pending, and nothing reaches the agent until you run `chimera plugin enable`. Then its skills, commands and agents appear namespaced (`plugin:name`) as untrusted text: agents follow project-agent rules, Claude Code tool names are translated and can only narrow, `allowed-tools` and `model` are ignored, and expanding a plugin command marks the run as tainted. Hooks, `bin/` and monitors stay inert; an MCP server is added only when you name it, through the pinned-manifest hold. An update that changes the manifest, hooks, servers or tools holds the plugin with the diff. `plugin:<name>` joins the deployment policy, and bots, cron, `serve` and guests get no plugin unless `CHIMERA_UNATTENDED_PLUGINS` lists it. (#971)

- **The parallel-batch panel can be minimised, moved and closed, and each task's answer reaches you.** "Gerenciador de Agentes" now uses the same panel frame as the side panels (drag, move to a dock or back to the main column, minimise to a summary, close to a "Batch" chip that reopens it); hiding it never stops the batch, only Stop and Stop all do. Each task's final answer and how it ended are shown on its card (an analysis task reads "answered, no edits"), and the finished batch is recorded in the Code conversation, fenced as an agents' report; an answer from a task that read untrusted content marks the next turn as tainted. (#974)

- **The MCP bridge opens a conversation inside a project.** `desktop_send` takes `project` (a registered project or a known repository), and `worktree: "new"` with an optional `branch`: Chimera creates and owns the worktree beside the repository (`.chimera-worktrees/<repo>/`, never the temp folder), the conversation groups under the project, and the cleanup dialog removes it after the merge. Unknown projects, paths outside the project and run-branch names are refused, and a new worktree does not inherit the project's shell grant. Conversation worktrees now survive restarts: the storage card's orphan sweep no longer removes them. (#975)

- **Settings › Plugins: see, add and switch on plugins.** *Mine* lists each installed plugin with its status, source and pin, a capability line (instructions only, starts N MCP servers, reaches the network, brings hooks: inert), its components, update with a diff and remove. *Discover* lists the marketplaces you added, with search and filters by category and by what a plugin runs; entries that are not pinned stay visible with the reason. *+ Add* takes a GitHub marketplace pinned to a commit, a local folder or a .zip. Switching a plugin on shows what will reach the agent and asks for each MCP server separately, and only you can do it: the MCP bridge can list, validate and install pending, never enable, remove or add marketplaces. (#976)

### Changed

- **The Code sidebar groups conversations by project, like the Claude desktop app.** A repository's worktrees fall under the repository (a switch turns this off), each project has a collapsible header with a + for a new conversation there, a ⑂ count of its worktrees and a ⋯ menu (open, collapse, rename, hide, delete, clean up finished worktrees). Rows show the title and, under it, branch and time; five per project with "show more"; a search over title, branch and project; status filters only when they have counts. (#970)

### Fixed

- **The Code screen's side panel shows only cards that have something to show.** Tools, Tokens, Memory and Fusion used to draw an empty frame with a dash; they now appear when data arrives. Titles are no longer forced to upper case and are no longer cut, the move/maximize/minimize controls appear on hover or focus, and a layout that was never customised gets a new default order. (#964)

- **Approving with a click works again after you reopen the app.** A background service the current app did not start holds no screen credential, so every click was refused until you restarted the service from the tray. The app now restarts such a service by itself: at once when it is idle, and as soon as running work ends when it is busy, without asking. While it waits, the approval card says so and offers approving with the code from a terminal or an explicit "Restart now" that warns it stops running turns. (#972)

name: v0.68.1
body:
### Fixed

- **The desktop app starts again.** In 0.68.0 its backend died at start on every machine with `No module named 'chimera.cli.commands.apilogs'`: the CLI imports its command areas by name, PyInstaller follows only import statements, and the freeze left that area out. The freeze now collects every chimera module, and the release starts the frozen backend and requires an HTTP answer before it ships. (#962)

name: v0.68.0
body:
> ⚠️ **Do not install this release.** The desktop app's backend fails to start: the PyInstaller freeze left out `chimera.cli.commands.apilogs`, which the CLI imports by name (`ModuleNotFoundError`). Install [v0.68.1](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/releases/tag/v0.68.1), which fixes it. The PyPI package is not affected.

### Added

- **MCP servers can be paused without losing configuration.** `chimera mcp disable/enable` preserves the server and its approved manifest while excluding disabled servers from connection and agent mounts; local stdio servers also support `--cwd`, runtime `{env:NAME}` references and a separate `--catalog-timeout`.

- **Optional provider-bound image resizing.** Vision attachments are reduced to configured dimension and base64-size limits when Pillow is available; originals remain unchanged, and resized dimensions are recorded in the turn receipt.

- **The Code agent can ask the user a bounded question.** `ask_user` pauses an attended Code turn for an option or free-text answer, returns an explicit no-response result on timeout, and remains a distinct data-only kind that cannot approve a governed action. Terminal, bot, and unattended turns do not register it.

- **Global and nested `AGENTS.md` instructions are reloaded with receipt provenance.** Owner guidance from `CHIMERA_HOME/AGENTS.md` precedes project rules; focused nested files share the existing character budget, and changed instruction versions are announced without copying their contents into the receipt.
